title: QBR: Inference Health, Runway & Sprint Commitments
summary: Quarterly health review covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents in the last quarter, and alignment on pilot sprint commitments. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share Dedicated capacity quote, security artifact packet, and run a 48-hour latency/cost benchmark with Maya's sample traffic. Customer to confirm budget window and internal stakeholders for pilot gating.

unexpected latency spike investigation (late Feb outage)
Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs and pricing

pilot scope: 2-week load bench, success criteria
roadmap alignment: model rollouts and canary strategy

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-21 15:00 UTC — Duration 1h18m; Attendees: Alicia, Samir, Jordan (Redwood); Maya, Carlos, Priya, Evan (Nebula)

[00:00] Alicia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — usage, recent reliability incident, Dedicated options, security asks, and pilot commitments. Maya, want to start with how things have been on your side?

[00:18] Maya (Product): Yeah, sure. Uh, thanks. So overall usage has trended up, we're seeing a 32% month-on-month for chat generation and embeddings are, um, steady but growing when we do recommendations. The big thing was that late February latency spike — that caught us out.

[00:40] Carlos (Eng): Right, the spike — for us it looked like tail latency went to 2.3s at peak for short sessions. That bounced after autoscale but had an impact on our frontend errors. We opened an internal postmortem.

[00:56] Samir (SE): Thanks, do you have the trace IDs? We pulled a few from logs; early signs point to a cold-KV-cache miss with a very high prefix fan-out. Our runtime falls back to eager KV loads which can add overhead.

[01:12] Carlos: We shared traces in the ticket, but some of the service tags got munged (the kuber name was different), so it's been a bit messy.

[01:30] Maya: And to be clear — it's not just latency, it affected our conversion funnel for, like, a 3 hour window. We're aligned that it's high priority.

[01:45] Alicia: Understood. On the Reliability side we ran a fast root-cause — there's an interaction between prefix caching and our batching policy when sequences are long and the batch aggregator tries to coalesce heterogeneous seq lengths. We recommended a temporary change to reduce max batch wait to hit SLOs, but that increases token cost. Tradeoff.

[02:05] Priya (Head of ML): Cost is something we want to nail down. Evan, finance side — how flexible is the runway?

[02:12] Evan (Finance): We're in a budget window mid-April. We can commit to a pilot spend but need a clear expected unit-cost. Show us delta between Hosted baseline and Dedicated commit scenarios.

[02:30] Samir: We'll produce a model-level cost split — we can show token cost, infra overhead, and amortized KV cache savings for Dedicated pools. Note: Dedicated allows longer-lived KV caches, reduces cold starts, and with our autoscale policies you often get better P50/P95 latency at a lower total cost per useful-req.

[02:55] Maya: Is quantization going to affect quality? We tried a 4-bit variant and saw some regressions for our domain prompts.

[03:05] Samir: Yeah, quantization is model and prompt dependent. We recommend a small eval harness before rolling a 4-bit quant to production. Redwood Optimize can run differential evals and flag quality regressions against your prompt set.

[03:25] Carlos: For private deployments, we still need SSO and KMS integration. The security team will want a list of artifacts.

[03:33] Jordan (CSM): We have a security packet — SOC2 report, architecture diagram for VPC peering, and KMS integration notes. Samir will attach those.

[03:45] Maya: Great. And we need demo of canary rollback for model rollouts — we want to test a new model with 5% traffic then increase.

[03:55] Alicia: Canary + automatic fallback is supported. You can pin versions and create A/B rollouts, and you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if latency or error rate thresholds breach. We'll share a sample policy.

[04:12] Evan: On procurement, what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated? If we commit, do we get reserved GPU pools we can rely on?

[04:22] Samir: Typical minimum is a 3-month reserved capacity for pilot, but we can do month-to-month for trials with burst capacity. Reserved capacity gives you guaranteed throughput and priority routing. We'll show a few commit tiers in the quote.

[04:40] Maya: About the bench — we want Redwood to run a 48-hour realistic traffic bench using our sample data to measure P50/P95, token cost, and KV hit ratios. If we see >15% cost savings on Dedicated with comparable quality and lower tail latency, that's a win.

[05:02] Samir: Agree. We can do that. Need the sample traffic (anonymized) and a definition of success. Also want to coordinate model versions to test: your current live model and the candidate.

[05:18] Maya: I'll send the sample and success metrics. Also, quick ask — can you include audit-log retention options? Our security requires 90-day immutable logs for a pilot.

[05:28] Jordan: We offer configurable retention and can integrate with your SIEM via streaming. We'll include retention tiers in the security doc.

[05:40] Carlos: Need to talk about the Feb outage — is Redwood going to add more observability into token-level tracing? We want to trace a user transaction end-to-end.

[05:50] Samir: We can provide token-level breakdowns and route-level flame charts in the console, plus sampling hooks for distributed tracing. We'll also include a quickstart for instrumentation.

[06:04] Maya: OK let's talk timeline. If we can get artifacts and quote by Thursday (3/25), and run the bench the following week, we could make a mid-April decision.

[06:16] Alicia: That's feasible. To recap: Redwood will send pricing scenarios, security packet, sample runbook for canary/fallback, and run a 48-hr bench using customer's sample traffic. Customer to confirm budget and provide traffic.

[06:30] Evan: Finance will review the delta. Also one more — any concerns around data residency? We need logs and PII to remain in us-east-1 for now.

[06:40] Samir: We support region pinning for Hosted and Private deployments; logs can be routed to your KMS in region. We'll document data flows.

[06:50] Maya: Quick note: we also trialed competitor X's managed offering — they were cheaper upfront but had worse tail-latency. So we're open to Dedicated if the cost model is clearer.

[07:05] Carlos: Technical note — our inference payloads have variable seq-len; can we tune the batcher to avoid cross-traffic padding?

[07:12] Samir: Yes, we have workload-aware batching policies; plus you can set max padding thresholds and per-route batching hints. We'll push recommended values after reviewing sample traces.

[07:30] Jordan: I'll add a small playbook for fallbacks and escalation contacts.

[07:38] Maya: Thanks everyone. Any final Qs?

[07:45] Alicia: None from me. We'll follow up with the docs and the tailored quote.

[07:50] Evan: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.

[07:55] Meeting end: Recap and adjourn.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard technical terms (e.g., "kay vee cache" written as KV, "quantizaion" typo in one clip), speaker overlap in a few segments around 05:00 when multiple people chimed in.
